align_frames — ASTROSTACK align op

• Data kinds: images → images

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.align_frames(frames, reference=0, order=3, **align_kw) (to call the implementation directly, import astrostack; astrostack.align_frames(frames, reference=0, order=3, **align_kw); from the registry, opsastrostack.get("align_frames"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.align_frames(...) returns only the declared out type images (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.align_frames.raw(...) or call astrostack.align_frames directly.

• Underlying return: (aligned, matrices) -> images

Usage

Register a series of frames onto one reference.

For each frame the transform is estimated with frame_align, and scipy.ndimage.affine_transform performs inverse mapping and resampling.

An honest caveat: interpolation does not preserve the image. Noise-free 64x64 / 12 stars, shifted by (0.5, 0.5) px and shifted back, measured::

order=1 (bilinear) total flux -0.016 % star peak -11.437 %

order=3 (spline) total flux -0.016 % star peak -0.312 %

Total flux is almost preserved either way, yet with bilinear the star peak drops by more than a tenth —— a 0.5 px shift is the worst phase for bilinear, since it becomes a simple mean of the 4 neighbouring pixels. The default is order=3 because of this measurement (order=3 creates a tiny negative rim around stars, but in the measurement above the minimum was -0.0000, not a visible amount).

If you want to keep both flux and peak exactly, do not interpolate: pass to drizzle_resample —— not interpolating is drizzle's very reason for existing. However,

do not pass the estimated shifts as-is: the translation of the matrices returned here points "back to the reference", the opposite sign of what drizzle needs. Pass them through drizzle_shifts::

aligned, mats = align_frames(frames)

sci, wht = drizzle_resample(frames, drizzle_shifts(mats), scale=2.0)

Returns (aligned, matrices):

• aligned —— list of length N, each (H, W) float64 (images vocabulary). The reference frame is returned as-is without transformation (even the identity transform blurs the image through interpolation, so there is no reason to pass it through).

• matrices —— list of length N, each (3, 3). The reference gets the identity matrix.

Raises ValueError: if *frames* is not a list / tuple / fewer than 2 frames / *reference* is out of range / *order* is outside 0 to 5 / frame_align fails on any 1 frame (a failure is not silently turned into the identity).
